newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to name Asian-American to top Justice post.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to name Asian-American to top Justice post.

text.p: President Bill Clinton plans to name California lawyer Bill Lann Lee to be assistant attorney general for civil rights, making him the first Asian-American to hold that post, the White House said on Thursday.

Lee, 48, the son of immigrants who is now director of the western regional office of the Legal Defence and Educational Fund of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP), would succeed Deval Patrick.

In confirming a New York Times report on Lee's prospective nomination, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said that later on Thursday Clinton would make public the names of those who will serve on a new blue-ribbon panel that is to examine the state of U.S race relations.

Clinton, who wants to leave his mark in history as a president who worked for racial and ethnic harmony in the United States, will make a major speech on the issue at the University of California at San Diego on Saturday.

Lee, regarded in legal circles as one of the nation's top civil rights lawyers, has helped lead a court challenge to a California referendum vote to ban affirmative action, the system of preferences to correct past race and gender bias.
As a result, his nomination could face opposition in the Senate from conservative Republicans who oppose affirmative action. Lee will require Senate confirmation.
The White House said Clinton also intended to nominate Raymond Fisher, another California lawyer, to be associate attorney general. That is the third highest post in the Justice Department.
Fisher, 57, is a private attorney who specialises in business and civil cases. He is perhaps best known as head of the Los Angeles Police Commission.
